newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Aromatics opens S$1 bln petchem complex.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Aromatics opens S$1 bln petchem complex.

text.p: Singapore Aromatics Co Pte Ltd (SAC) said on Monday it has officially opened its Singapore $1.0 billion world-scale petrochemical complex which assumes a key role in its joint venture's Asia Pacific business strategy.
"The project was completed on schedule, below budget and without any compromise in safety," Richard A. Marsteller, SAC's managing director said.
Established in 1994, SAC is a jont venture between Exxon Chemical Singapore Pte Ltd with a 50-percent share and Amoco Chemicals Holdings Co with 40-percent.
The remainder was held by China American Singapore Co Pte Ltd, an affiliate of Taiwanese China America Petrochemical Co (CAPCO), itself a joint venture between Amoco and state-owned

The complex has a capacity to produce 350,000 tonnes of paraxylene and 96,000 tonnes of benzene annually. Paraxylene is erepthalic acid (PTA), a key component in polyster production, while benzene is used to make styrene monomer, a feedstock for plastics and synthetic rubber.
Marsteller said paraxylene is one of the fastest growing products in petrochemicals. Asian demand accounts for about half the world's consumption and is growing strongly.
The complex, located on a 30-acre land on Pulau Ayer Chawan, an island off southwestern Singapore, was completed in November 1996. Commercial production started in mid-January.
Company sources early this year said SAC planned to cover 35 percent of its 1.5 million tonne per year naphtha feedstock demand on the spot and semi-term basis.
